Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — DeltaSelect selects a small fixed task set from repeated public benchmark trials (DeepSWE v1.1) by conservative one-run correlation, calibrates fractional F2P results to the full-score scale and fits a dollar budget, for baseline-versus-candidate comparisons during development; case study revising Agent Layer skills and instructions with gpt-5.6-luna low in Codex

Skill and instruction files bundled with Agent Layer (planning, plan review, implementation, delegation, review); for the method: a frozen experiment specification (ranked tasks, repetitions, calibration coefficients, weights, price assumptions, snapshot checksum, seeds)

Automatic: DeepSWE verifier records (F2P, P2P, binary); request-level token and billing telemetry; harness records task and environment checksums, client and model versions, reasoning effort. Statistics: 10,000 deterministic resamples (seeded from snapshot checksum), Welch-Satterthwaite test with variance transferred from published Luna medium runs, exact paired sign-flip test for cost

No success criterion stated by the author for any configuration judged on its own; the case-study goal was relative ('lower cost without sacrificing score', Table 1), so quality and cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors. On the 8 selected tasks, one run per task: (1) Codex + gpt-5.6-luna low, bare (baseline): calibrated score 20.43% (unchanged repeat 14.84%), $0.32; published mini-swe-agent estimate -0.54%, $0.13; (2) Codex + gpt-5.6-luna medium, bare: 45.50%, $1.34 (published 19.38%, $0.38); (3) Codex + gpt-5.6-luna high, bare (earlier, non-certified environment): 56.33%, $3.00 (published 53.34%, $2.04); (4) Agent Layer initial skills and instructions + Codex + gpt-5.6-luna low: 36.46%, $4.18, F2P 251/411, 55 model calls; (5) Agent Layer adopted skills and instructions (evaluation 13) + Codex + gpt-5.6-luna low: 42.36%, $1.75, F2P 265/411, 37 calls; intermediate revisions scored 23.15-43.72% at $1.76-2.64 where costs are reported (evaluations 6 and 7 were cheaper than $1.76, values not given). Published-data projection: Claude Opus 5 medium vs Gemini 3.6 Flash high distinguished with 9 tasks at $113.08 (p=0.0473) vs $3,063.63 for the full protocol

rev.why: Cost range of intermediate revisions was wrong: evaluations 6 and 7 were 'cheaper' than evaluation 5 ($1.76), so $1.76 is not the lower bound (p. 17). The verdict wording 'cost verdict judged by the author against that goal' gave no verdict; the only criterion is relative to the initial version, so it is unclear whether it counts as a success criterion under the 2026-11-23 rule.

fields.warn: O autor só dá um objetivo relativo (custo menor sem perder score face à versão inicial). Decide se isto conta como critério de sucesso para dar veredicto à versão adotada ou se fica 'no criterion stated'. O valor foi corrigido na verificação 1; confirma-o no texto.

fields.v: Tasks: 8 DeepSWE tasks selected under a $0.65 one-run budget for published gpt-5.6-luna low. Configurations: bare Codex at three reasoning levels vs published mini-swe-agent; Agent Layer skill revisions (10 configurations, 13 evaluations). Held constant: model gpt-5.6-luna low, Codex harness, tasks, calibration, weights, repetitions, task and environment checksums (low and medium only). Baseline: bare Codex Luna low and the initial skills version. Acceptance tests: DeepSWE verifier tests. Repetitions: one run per task; three configurations repeated once. Human intervention: none during runs; author decides adoption

Adopted vs initial skills: cost -$2.43 (-58.1%), lower on all 8 tasks (exact sign-flip p=0.008); calibrated score +5.90 pp (42.36% vs 36.46%), not significant (SE 5.90 points, Welch df 29.23, p=0.326 with transferred variance). Initial skills beat bare Codex Luna low (36.46% vs 20.43%) at 13x the cost; bare Luna medium scored 45.50% at $1.34, above the adopted skills. Codex scores were 21.0, 26.1 and 3.0 points above published mini-swe-agent estimates and cost 1.5-3.5x more. Only 22 of 113 DeepSWE tasks (19.5%) had fifth-percentile one-run correlation >= 0.50

Author: the fixed task set gave a stable measurement and diagnosable transcripts across iterations; projected to distinguish a known 20.3-point gap at 27.1x lower cost. Limits: selector not compared with random, cheapest-first or median-correlation selection at equal cost; value of fractional scoring, calibration and weighting not isolated; in-sample (same snapshot for ranking and example); one run per task in Codex, variance transferred from mini-swe-agent; repeated configurations moved 0.7-4.3 points; published results do not transfer across harnesses

Small fixed set cannot cover full benchmark capabilities and risks specialization to selected tasks; small sets magnify broken tasks; selector and scoring choices need direct comparisons; OLS may fit poorly at the extremes; related tasks violate independence; evidence from one DeepSWE snapshot, one model family and one custom harness; several evaluations changed more than one instruction, so the 58.1% cost reduction cannot be attributed to a single edit. Future: matched-cost selector comparisons, nonlinear calibration, covariance-aware methods

Tool and source: https://agent-layer.dev/deltaselect, https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer (pinned DeepSWE data included). Values from Table 1 and text. Reporting points: Figure 5 cost differences (+$0.95, +$0.97) differ by 1 cent from the text values ($0.38 -> $1.34, $2.04 -> $3.00); the high-reasoning Codex run predates the environment checksum control; one DeepSWE task has three trials for Gemini. Comparison chosen retrospectively, explicitly not preregistered (p. 10). Programming languages: not stated (DeepSWE repositories in TypeScript/JavaScript, Rust, Go, Python inferred from task names)
